late: Assessment Policy. Assignments are due at 11:59 PM on the date stated in the course outline. Late submission is normally penalized by ten percent for each day after the deadline. Illness extensions require medical evidence before the deadline. Students must send the certificate to the course coordinator and wait for a written reply before assuming that an extension has been granted. Extensions are not given for travel plans or for a heavy workload in other courses. Group projects follow the same rule, and each member must report any illness separately to the coordinator. When a student submits work after the final accepted date, the coordinator records the submission time, compares it with the approved extension if there is one, applies the penalty for every full day of delay, and sends the final mark to the student together with a short note explaining how the penalty was calculated. Students may ask for a review of the penalty within five working days. Marks are published on the learning portal after all submissions have been checked.
password: IT Help Guide. Every student receives one university account that is used for email, the learning portal and the library. Reset a forgotten password using the recovery link. The link is shown on the login page and is sent to the registered phone number or the alternate email address. Never share recovery codes with anyone, including friends, classmates or staff. Accounts locked after five failed attempts cannot use the recovery link and must be unlocked by the help desk. The help desk asks for the student card and a short description of the problem, and it does not ask for the current password at any time. After a successful reset the student should log out of all shared computers, choose a new password that has at least twelve characters, and avoid using the same password for personal accounts outside the university. Passwords expire every one hundred and eighty days, and a reminder is sent fourteen days before the expiry date.
assignment: Submission Guide. Each course uses the same method for handing in written work so that files are never lost. Upload assignments through the learning portal. Submit the final file as a PDF and write the course code and student number in the file name. Students who cannot access the portal may email the file to the coordinator before the deadline and must keep the sent message as proof. The portal accepts files up to twenty megabytes, and larger files should be compressed or split into two parts that are clearly numbered. Each upload creates a receipt that shows the date and time, and students should save this receipt until the final marks are published. Only the latest upload before the deadline is marked, so a student may replace an earlier file as many times as needed. Source code, data files and images must be placed in one folder and submitted as a single archive together with the report. Plagiarism checks run automatically on every upload.
contractor: Remote Work Policy. This policy explains where staff and contractors may work and how requests are approved. Employees may work remotely up to three days each week with the approval of their manager. Contractors can work remotely only if the signed contract permits it. Employee rules do not apply to contractors, so a manager cannot approve remote work for a contractor on a verbal basis. A contractor whose contract is silent on the matter must work from the office until the contract is amended in writing by the human resources office. Version one of this policy, which is now withdrawn, allowed contractors to work remotely for two days each week without any contract clause, and any older copy that says this must not be used. Requests for an amendment are sent to the human resources office together with the contract number, and the office replies within ten working days. Remote workers must stay reachable during office hours, use only approved company laptops, and connect through the secure network at all times.
printer: Printer Troubleshooting Guide. This guide covers the shared office printers on every floor and the most common faults reported to the help desk. For blank printer pages, check ink levels and run the cleaning utility. Print a test page afterwards to confirm that the fault is fixed, and note the result in the maintenance log. If the test page is still blank, remove the cartridge, check the protective tape and place it back firmly before trying again. For a blank scanner image, which is a different fault, check the document placement and select the correct scanning source instead of using these steps. Older laser models in the storage room use a drum unit, and for those models the guide says to replace the drum when pages are blank, but this advice does not apply to the current inkjet printers. Never open the printer while it is printing, and always switch the device off before removing a jammed sheet. Report any repeated fault to the help desk with the printer label and the time of the failure.
